description: All Other Miscellaneous Waste Management Services

This sector encompasses establishments providing instruction and training in diverse subjects, from schools and colleges to universities and training centers. Services may include academic, technical, and specialized instruction delivered in various settings.

This subsector provides instruction and training across diverse subjects, from elementary schools to universities and specialized training centers. The structure is based on educational level and type of service, with varying instructor training requirements.
This industry group furnishes academic courses and associated coursework for basic preparatory education (kindergarten through 12th grade), including school boards and districts.

This industry furnishes academic courses and associated coursework for basic preparatory education (kindergarten through 12th grade). It includes school boards, school districts, charter schools, and schools for physically disabled.

This industry group furnishes academic or academic and technical courses, granting associate degrees, certificates, or diplomas below the baccalaureate level. Admission requires at least a high school diploma or equivalent.

This industry furnishes academic or academic and technical courses, granting associate degrees, certificates, or diplomas below the baccalaureate level. Admission requires at least a high school diploma or equivalent.

This industry group furnishes academic courses and grants baccalaureate or graduate degrees. Admission requires at least a high school diploma or equivalent, with instruction offered in diverse settings and methods.

This industry furnishes academic courses and grants baccalaureate or graduate degrees. Admission requires at least a high school diploma or equivalent, with instruction offered in diverse settings and methods, e.g., military academies, theological seminaries.

formal_name: Business Schools and Computer and Management Training
description: This industry group offers courses in office procedures, secretarial/stenographic skills, computer training (excluding repair), and short-duration courses/seminars for management/professional development. Instruction is provided in diverse settings using various methods, including simulators.

This industry offers courses in office procedures, secretarial/stenographic skills, and basic office skills (e.g., word processing). It also provides classes in office machine operation, reception, communications, and other skills for clerical/secretarial careers.

This industry conducts computer training (excluding computer repair) in programming, software applications, computerized business systems, electronics technology, computer operations, and LAN management. Instruction is provided in diverse settings and methods, including simulators.

This industry offers short-duration courses and seminars for management and professional development, provided directly to individuals or through employer programs. Courses can be customized and utilize diverse instruction settings and methods, including simulators.

This industry group offers vocational and technical training in subjects and trades leading to job-specific certification. Instruction is structured and specialized, covering areas like cosmetology, aviation, and various trades, using diverse methods including simulators.

This industry offers job or career vocational/technical courses (excluding cosmetology, barber, aviation/flight, and apprenticeship training). Curriculums are highly structured, specialized, and lead to job-specific certification, e.g., bartending, broadcasting, computer repair, truck driving, graphic arts, and real estate.

This industry group offers diverse instruction (excluding academic, business, computer, management, technical/trade). It includes fine arts, sports, recreation, language, exam preparation, tutoring, and automobile driving instruction, provided in various settings and methods.

This industry offers instruction in the arts, e.g., dance, art, drama, and music, including dance studios, music schools, performing arts schools (excluding academic), and photography schools (excluding commercial).

This industry offers instruction in athletic activities, including camps and schools. It encompasses overnight/day sports instruction camps, professional sports instructors (non-participating), cheerleading, gymnastics, martial arts, riding, and swimming instruction.
This industry offers foreign language instruction (including sign language), from conversational skills for personal enrichment to intensive training courses for career or educational opportunities.

This industry offers instruction (excluding academic schools, colleges, universities, business/computer/management, technical/trade, fine arts, sports, recreation, language, exam preparation, tutoring, and automobile driving instruction). Examples include public speaking training, survival training, and speed reading instruction.

formal_name: All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction
description: All Other Miscellaneous Schools and Instruction

This industry group provides non-instructional services supporting educational processes or systems, e.g., educational consultants, testing services, guidance counseling, and student exchange programs.
This industry provides non-instructional services supporting educational processes or systems, e.g., educational consultants, testing services, guidance counseling, and student exchange programs.

This sector delivers health care and social assistance services to individuals, ranging from medical care (e.g., hospitals, outpatient clinics) to social support (e.g., family services, community housing). Services are provided by trained professionals, often with a mix of health and social service components.

This subsector delivers direct or indirect health care services to ambulatory patients, typically not providing inpatient services. Health practitioners in this area focus on outpatient services, where facilities and equipment are not the most significant part of the production process.

This industry group includes offices of licensed physicians (M.D. or D.O.) practicing general or specialized medicine/surgery independently, in their own offices or facilities of others. It distinguishes between mental health specialists and all other physicians.

This industry comprises establishments of health practitioners having the degree of M.D. (Doctor of Medicine) or D.O. (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine) primarily engaged in the independent practice of general or specialized medicine (except psychiatry or psychoanalysis) or surgery.  These practitioners operate private or group practices in their own offices (e.g., centers, clinics) or in the facilities of others, such as hospitals or HMO medical centers.

formal_name: Offices of Physicians (except Mental Health Specialists)
description: This industry comprises establishments of health practitioners having the degree of M.D. (Doctor of Medicine) or D.O. (Doctor of Osteopathic Medicine) primarily engaged in the independent practice of general or specialized medicine (excluding psychiatry or psychoanalysis) or surgery. These practitioners operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

formal_name: Offices of Physicians, Mental Health Specialists
description: This industry comprises establishments of health practitioners (M.D. or D.O.) primarily engaged in the independent practice of psychiatry or psychoanalysis. These practitioners operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

This industry group includes offices of licensed dentists (D.M.D., D.D.S., or D.D.Sc.) practicing general or specialized dentistry/dental surgery independently, in their own offices or facilities of others. Services range from preventive to emergency care.

This industry comprises establishments of licensed dentists (D.M.D., D.D.S., or D.D.Sc.) primarily practicing general or specialized dentistry/dental surgery independently, in their own offices or facilities of others. They provide comprehensive preventive, cosmetic, or emergency care, or specialize in a single field.

This industry group comprises offices of independent health practitioners (excluding physicians and dentists). It includes chiropractors, optometrists, mental health specialists, physical/occupational/speech therapists, audiologists, podiatrists, acupuncturists, and other miscellaneous health practitioners.

This industry comprises establishments of licensed chiropractors (D.C.) primarily practicing chiropractic, providing diagnostic/therapeutic treatment of neuromusculoskeletal disorders through spinal/extremity manipulation. They operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

This industry comprises establishments of licensed optometrists (O.D.) primarily practicing optometry, examining, diagnosing, treating, and managing visual system disorders. They prescribe/provide eyeglasses, contact lenses, low vision aids, and vision therapy, and may offer optician services.

formal_name: Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)
description: Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)

formal_name: Offices of Mental Health Practitioners (except Physicians)
description: This industry comprises establishments of independent mental health practitioners (excluding physicians) primarily diagnosing/treating mental/emotional/behavioral disorders and/or individual/group social dysfunction. They operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

formal_name: Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists
description: Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists

formal_name: Offices of Physical, Occupational and Speech Therapists, and Audiologists
description: This industry comprises establishments of independent health practitioners providing physical therapy, occupational therapy (helping regain physical/mental functioning), and speech/language/hearing diagnosis/treatment. They operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

formal_name: Offices of All Other Health Practitioners
description: Offices of All Other Health Practitioners

This industry comprises establishments of licensed podiatrists (D.P.M.) primarily practicing podiatry, diagnosing and treating diseases/deformities of the foot. They operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

formal_name: Offices of All Other Miscellaneous Health Practitioners
description: This industry comprises establishments of independent health practitioners (excluding physicians, dentists, chiropractors, optometrists, mental health specialists, physical/occupational/speech therapists, audiologists, and podiatrists). They operate private/group practices in their own offices or facilities of others.

This industry group includes establishments with medical staff providing a range of outpatient services. It covers family planning, mental health/substance abuse treatment, HMO medical centers, kidney dialysis centers, freestanding ambulatory surgical/emergency centers, and other general or specialized outpatient care.

This industry provides a range of outpatient family planning services, e.g., contraceptive services, genetic/prenatal counseling, voluntary sterilization, and therapeutic/medically induced termination of pregnancy.

formal_name: Outpatient Mental Health and Substance Abuse Centers
description: Outpatient Mental Health and Substance Abuse Centers

formal_name: Outpatient Mental Health and Substance Abuse Centers
description: This industry provides outpatient services for diagnosing/treating mental health disorders and alcohol/substance abuse, typically for patients not requiring inpatient treatment. They offer counseling and information, or refer to more extensive programs.

This industry comprises HMO-owned establishments with physicians/medical staff primarily providing outpatient medical services to HMO subscribers, focusing on primary health care. It includes HMOs that both provide health care and underwrite health/medical insurance policies.
This industry comprises establishments with medical staff primarily providing outpatient kidney or renal dialysis services.

formal_name: Freestanding Ambulatory Surgical and Emergency Centers
description: This industry provides outpatient surgical services (e.g., orthoscopic, cataract surgery) or emergency care (e.g., setting broken bones, treating lacerations) on an outpatient basis. Establishments have specialized facilities and equipment like operating/recovery rooms and anesthetic/X-ray equipment.

This industry provides general or specialized outpatient care (excluding family planning, mental health/substance abuse, HMO medical centers, kidney dialysis centers, and freestanding surgical/emergency centers). It includes centers/clinics of health practitioners with different degrees practicing within the same establishment.

This industry group, known as medical and diagnostic laboratories, provides analytic or diagnostic services, including body fluid analysis and diagnostic imaging, generally on referral from a health practitioner.

This industry, known as medical laboratories, provides analytic or diagnostic services, including body fluid analysis, generally to the medical profession or on referral from a health practitioner. Examples include blood analysis, medical pathology, and forensic laboratories.

This industry, known as diagnostic imaging centers, produces images of patients, generally on referral from a health practitioner. Examples include CT-scan, medical radiological, dental/medical X-ray, ultrasound, and MRI centers.

This industry group provides skilled nursing services in the home, along with a range of personal care, homemaker, physical therapy, medical social, and high-tech care services. It includes home health care agencies, visiting nurse associations, and in-home hospice care.

This industry provides skilled nursing services in the home, along with a range of personal care, homemaker, physical therapy, medical social services, medications, medical equipment, counseling, and high-tech care like intravenous therapy.

This industry group provides ambulatory health care services (excluding offices of practitioners, outpatient centers, laboratories, home health care, and ambulances). It includes blood/organ banks, health screening, and pacemaker monitoring services.

This industry transports patients by ground or air, along with medical care. Services are often provided during medical emergencies but not restricted to them, utilizing vehicles equipped with lifesaving equipment operated by medically trained personnel.

formal_name: All Other Ambulatory Health Care Services
description: All Other Ambulatory Health Care Services
This industry collects, stores, and distributes blood and blood products, and stores and distributes body organs.

formal_name: All Other Miscellaneous Ambulatory Health Care Services
description: This industry provides ambulatory health care services (excluding offices of physicians, dentists, other health practitioners, outpatient care centers, medical/diagnostic laboratories, home health care, ambulances, blood/organ banks). Examples include health screening, hearing testing, pacemaker monitoring, and smoking cessation programs.

This subsector provides medical, diagnostic, and treatment services, including physician, nursing, and other health services to inpatients. Hospitals offer specialized accommodation and rely on facilities and equipment as integral parts of their production process.

This industry group operates licensed general medical and surgical hospitals, providing diagnostic and medical treatment (surgical and nonsurgical) to inpatients with diverse conditions. Services include outpatient care, laboratory, X-ray, and pharmacy.

This industry operates licensed general medical/surgical hospitals, providing diagnostic and medical treatment (surgical/nonsurgical) to inpatients with diverse conditions. Hospitals maintain beds, provide food, and have an organized staff of physicians/medical staff, usually offering outpatient, laboratory, X-ray, and pharmacy services.

This industry group operates licensed psychiatric and substance abuse hospitals, providing diagnostic, medical treatment, and monitoring services for inpatients with mental illness or substance abuse disorders. Services include psychiatric, psychological, and social work.

This industry operates licensed psychiatric and substance abuse hospitals, providing diagnostic, medical treatment, and monitoring for inpatients with mental illness or substance abuse disorders, often requiring extended stays. Services include psychiatric, psychological, and social work, with typical outpatient, laboratory, and X-ray services.

formal_name: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
description: This industry group operates licensed specialty hospitals (excluding psychiatric/substance abuse), providing diagnostic and medical treatment to inpatients with specific diseases or conditions. It includes long-term care, rehabilitation, and restorative services.

formal_name: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
description: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals

formal_name: Specialty (except Psychiatric and Substance Abuse) Hospitals
description: This industry operates licensed specialty hospitals (excluding psychiatric/substance abuse), providing diagnostic and medical treatment to inpatients with specific diseases/conditions. It includes long-term care for the chronically ill and rehabilitation services for physically challenged individuals, offering various support services.

This subsector provides residential care combined with nursing, supervisory, or other care as needed by residents. Facilities are a significant part of the production process, offering a mix of health and social services, often with substantial nursing components.

This industry group provides inpatient nursing and rehabilitative services for extended periods to individuals requiring continuous nursing care. Establishments have a permanent staff of registered or licensed practical nurses, e.g., convalescent homes, nursing homes, inpatient hospices.

This industry provides inpatient nursing and rehabilitative services for extended periods to individuals requiring nursing care. Establishments have a permanent core staff of registered/licensed practical nurses and other staff for continuous personal care, e.g., convalescent homes and inpatient hospices.

formal_name: Residential Intellectual and Developmental Disability, Mental Health, and Substance Abuse Facilities
description: This industry group provides residential care for persons with intellectual/developmental disabilities, mental health, or substance abuse problems. Facilities offer room, board, supervision, and counseling, with medical services being incidental to mental rehabilitation and support.

formal_name: Residential Intellectual and Developmental Disability Facilities
description: Residential Intellectual and Developmental Disability Facilities

formal_name: Residential Intellectual and Developmental Disability Facilities
description: This industry (e.g., group homes, hospitals, intermediate care facilities) provides residential care services for persons with intellectual and developmental disabilities. Facilities offer room, board, protective supervision, and counseling, with any health care being incidental.

formal_name: Residential Mental Health and Substance Abuse Facilities
description: Residential Mental Health and Substance Abuse Facilities

formal_name: Residential Mental Health and Substance Abuse Facilities
description: This industry provides residential care and treatment for patients with mental health and substance abuse illnesses, offering room, board, supervision, and counseling services. Medical services are incidental to the counseling, mental rehabilitation, and support services.

formal_name: Continuing Care Retirement Communities and Assisted Living Facilities for the Elderly
description: This industry group provides residential and personal care services for the elderly or persons unable/unwilling to live independently. Services include room, board, supervision, and daily living assistance, with or without on-site nursing care.

formal_name: Continuing Care Retirement Communities and Assisted Living Facilities for the Elderly
description: Continuing Care Retirement Communities and Assisted Living Facilities for the Elderly

This industry provides residential and personal care services with on-site nursing care facilities for the elderly or persons unable/unwilling to live independently. Residents live in various settings with meals, housekeeping, social, leisure, and other daily living assistance services.

formal_name: Assisted Living Facilities for the Elderly
description: This industry provides residential and personal care services (without nursing care) for the elderly or persons unable/unwilling to live independently. Care typically includes room, board, supervision, and assistance in daily living, e.g., housekeeping.

This industry group provides residential care (excluding intellectual/developmental disability, mental health/substance abuse, continuing care retirement, and assisted living facilities for the elderly). It offers supervision and personal care services, e.g., boot camps for youth, group homes for disabled, or orphanages.

This industry provides residential care (excluding intellectual/developmental disability, mental health/substance abuse, continuing care retirement, and assisted living facilities for the elderly). It also provides supervision and personal care services, e.g., boot/disciplinary camps for delinquent youth, group homes for disabled, and orphanages.

This subsector provides a wide variety of direct social assistance services to clients, excluding residential or accommodation services, except for short stays. These services encompass areas like child/youth support, elderly/disabled services, food/housing aid, and vocational rehabilitation.

This industry group provides nonresidential social assistance services to children, youth, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and other individuals/families. Services include adoption, foster care, drug prevention, life skills, day care, non-medical home care, crisis intervention, and counseling.

This industry provides nonresidential social assistance services for children and youth, focusing on adoption, foster care, drug prevention, life skills training, and positive social development, e.g., child guidance organizations and youth centers (excluding recreational only).

formal_name: Services for the Elderly and Persons with Disabilities
description: Services for the Elderly and Persons with Disabilities

formal_name: Services for the Elderly and Persons with Disabilities
description: This industry provides nonresidential social assistance services to improve quality of life for the elderly or persons with intellectual/developmental disabilities. Services include day care, non-medical home care/homemaker services, social activities, group support, and companionship.

This industry provides nonresidential individual and family social assistance services (excluding children, elderly, persons with disabilities). Examples include community action services, crisis intervention, family social services, hotline centers, marriage counseling, and telephone counseling.

formal_name: Community Food and Housing, and Emergency and Other Relief Services
description: This industry group collects, prepares, and delivers food for the needy; provides short-term emergency/temporary residential shelter; offers transitional housing; assists in volunteer construction/repair of low-cost housing; and provides relief services (food, shelter, clothing, medical) to disaster/conflict victims.

This industry collects, prepares, and delivers food for the needy. Establishments may distribute clothing/blankets, prepare/deliver meals to the ill/disabled, collect/distribute donated food, or provide meals at fixed/mobile locations, e.g., food banks, soup kitchens.

This industry provides short-term emergency shelter for victims of domestic violence, sexual assault, or child abuse, and/or temporary residential shelter for homeless individuals/families, runaway youth, and patients/families in medical crises. Shelters may be operated directly or housing subsidized.

This industry provides community housing services (excluding temporary shelters), e.g., transitional housing to low-income individuals, volunteer construction/repair of low-cost housing, and home repair for elderly/disabled homeowners. Establishments may subsidize housing or provide furniture/household supplies.
This industry provides food, shelter, clothing, medical relief, resettlement, and counseling to victims of domestic or international disasters or conflicts (e.g., wars).

This industry group provides vocational rehabilitation or habilitation services, e.g., job counseling, training, and work experience, to unemployed, underemployed, and disabled persons. It also trains and employs persons with disabilities, including sheltered workshops.

This industry provides vocational rehabilitation or habilitation services, e.g., job counseling, training, and work experience, to unemployed, underemployed, and disabled persons. It also provides training and employment to persons with disabilities, including sheltered workshops.

This industry group provides care and early learning for infants and children (birth through school age). Establishments may offer pre-kindergarten, kindergarten, or before/after-school educational programs, focusing on health, social, emotional learning, and family engagement.

This industry provides care and early learning opportunities for infants and children (birth through school age). It may offer pre-kindergarten, kindergarten, and/or before/after-school educational programs, focusing on health, social/emotional learning, and family engagement.

This sector provides cultural, entertainment, and recreational services. Activities include live performances (theater, music, sports), preserving/exhibiting historical sites and museums, and operating facilities for recreational activities like amusement parks, gambling, and sports centers.

formal_name: Performing Arts, Spectator Sports, and Related Industries
description: This subsector produces or organizes live performances, events, or exhibits, involving actors, singers, dancers, musicians, athletes, and other entertainers. It distinguishes producing events, organizing/promoting, managing entertainers, and providing artistic/technical skills for live events.
This industry group produces live theatrical presentations, e.g., musicals, operas, plays, comedy, dance, mime, puppet shows. Companies may or may not operate their own venues.

This industry comprises companies/groups/theaters producing live theatrical presentations (musicals, operas, plays, comedy, mime, puppet shows). It also includes dinner theaters producing live shows and providing food/beverages.

This industry comprises companies/groups/theaters producing all types of live theatrical dance presentations (e.g., ballet, contemporary dance, folk dance). Dance companies may or may not operate their own venues.

This industry produces live musical entertainment (excluding theatrical musical/opera productions) and includes independent (freelance) artists providing live musical entertainment. Groups/artists may perform live or in a studio, and may or may not operate their own facilities.

This industry comprises companies/groups (excluding theater companies, dance companies, musical groups/artists) primarily producing live theatrical presentations, e.g., carnival traveling shows, circuses, ice skating companies, and magic shows.

This industry group involves professional/semiprofessional sports teams/clubs participating in live events for paying audiences, operating racetracks without casinos, or independent athletes/owners participating in races. It also includes establishments supporting sports event participants.

This industry comprises professional or semiprofessional sports teams/clubs participating in live sporting events (e.g., baseball, basketball, football, hockey, soccer) before a paying audience. They may or may not operate their own arenas or stadiums.
This industry operates racetracks without casinos, and may also present/promote events like auto, dog, and horse races held in these facilities.

This industry includes independent athletes (golfers, boxers, race car drivers) participating in live sporting/racing events for a paying audience; owners of racing participants (cars, dogs, horses) entering them in events; and sports trainers providing specialized support services for competitors.

formal_name: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events
description: This industry group organizes, promotes, and/or manages live performing arts productions, sports events, and similar events (e.g., fairs, concerts, festivals). Promoters may manage/operate the facilities or use facilities managed by others.

formal_name: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events with Facilities
description: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events with Facilities

formal_name: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events with Facilities
description: This industry organizes, promotes, and/or manages live performing arts productions, sports events, and similar events (e.g., fairs, concerts, festivals) held in facilities they manage and operate. They may also manage/staff arenas, stadiums, or theaters for rent to other promoters.

formal_name: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities
description: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities

formal_name: Promoters of Performing Arts, Sports, and Similar Events without Facilities
description: This industry organizes, promotes, and/or manages live performing arts productions, sports events, and similar events (e.g., fairs, concerts, festivals) in facilities managed and operated by others. Theatrical (excluding motion picture) booking agencies are included.

formal_name: Agents and Managers for Artists, Athletes, Entertainers, and Other Public Figures
description: This industry group represents and/or manages creative/performing artists, sports figures, entertainers, and other public figures. Services include contract negotiations, financial management, and career promotion.

formal_name: Agents and Managers for Artists, Athletes, Entertainers, and Other Public Figures
description: Agents and Managers for Artists, Athletes, Entertainers, and Other Public Figures

formal_name: Agents and Managers for Artists, Athletes, Entertainers, and Other Public Figures
description: This industry represents and/or manages creative/performing artists, sports figures, entertainers, and other public figures. Services include contract negotiations, financial affairs management, and career promotion.

This industry group consists of independent (freelance) individuals performing in artistic productions, creating artistic/cultural works, or providing technical expertise for these productions. It also includes athletes/celebrities endorsing products or making public appearances for fees.

This industry comprises independent (freelance) individuals performing in artistic productions, creating artistic/cultural works, or providing technical expertise for these productions. It also includes athletes/celebrities endorsing products or making speeches/public appearances for a fee.

formal_name: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions
description: This subsector preserves and exhibits objects, sites, and natural wonders of historical, cultural, or educational value, like museums, historical sites, zoos, botanical gardens, and nature parks.

formal_name: Museums, Historical Sites, and Similar Institutions
description: This industry group preserves and exhibits objects, sites, and natural wonders of historical, cultural, and/or educational value. It includes art/science museums, historical sites, zoos, botanical gardens, and nature parks.

This industry preserves and exhibits objects of historical, cultural, and/or educational value, e.g., art galleries (excluding retail), art museums, halls of fame, planetariums, science/technology museums, and wax museums.

This industry preserves and exhibits sites, buildings, forts, or communities describing events/persons of historical interest. It includes archeological sites, battlefields, historical ships, and pioneer villages.
This industry preserves and exhibits live plant and animal life displays, e.g., aquariums, arboreta, aviaries, wild animal parks, and zoological gardens.

formal_name: Nature Parks and Other Similar Institutions
description: Nature Parks and Other Similar Institutions

formal_name: Nature Parks and Other Similar Institutions
description: This industry preserves and exhibits natural areas or settings, e.g., bird/wildlife sanctuaries, conservation areas, national parks, nature centers, and natural wonder tourist attractions (caverns, waterfalls).

This subsector operates facilities or provides services for sports, recreation, amusement, or gambling. It includes amusement parks, arcades, gambling establishments, golf courses, skiing facilities, marinas, fitness centers, and bowling centers.
This industry group operates amusement or theme parks with various attractions (rides, games, shows) and amusement arcades/parlors (excluding gambling, billiard, or pool).

This industry operates amusement or theme parks with various attractions, e.g., mechanical rides, water rides, games, shows, theme exhibits, refreshment stands, and picnic grounds. They may lease concession space.
This industry operates amusement (excluding gambling, billiard, or pool) arcades and parlors.

This industry group operates gambling facilities (excluding casino hotels) or provides gambling services. It includes casinos (without hotels), bingo halls, video gaming terminals, bookmakers, lotteries, and card rooms.

This industry operates gambling facilities (excluding casino hotels) offering table wagering games and other gambling activities like slot machines and sports betting. They often provide food and beverage services, and include floating casinos and casinos with racetracks.

This industry operates gambling facilities (excluding casinos/casino hotels) or provides gambling services. It includes bingo, off-track betting, slot machine parlors, bookmakers, lottery ticket sales agents (excluding retail stores), and card rooms.

This industry group provides recreational and amusement services (excluding amusement parks/arcades, gambling industries, golf courses/country clubs, skiing facilities, marinas, fitness centers, and bowling centers). It includes miniature golf, driving ranges, shooting ranges, recreational camps, and escape rooms.

This industry operates golf courses (excluding miniature) and/or country clubs with golf courses, dining, and other recreational facilities. They often provide food/beverage services, equipment rental, and golf instruction.

This industry operates downhill, cross-country, or related skiing areas and/or ski lifts/tows. They often provide food/beverage services, equipment rental, and ski instruction. Four-season resorts without accommodations are included.

This industry operates docking and/or storage facilities for pleasure craft owners, optionally with related activities like retailing fuel/marine supplies, and repairing, maintaining, or renting pleasure boats.

This industry operates fitness and recreational sports facilities for exercise and active physical fitness conditioning or recreational sports, e.g., swimming, skating, racquet sports. Examples include aerobic dance centers, gymnasiums, and handball clubs.
This industry operates bowling centers, often providing food and beverage services.

formal_name: All Other Amusement and Recreation Industries
description: All Other Amusement and Recreation Industries

formal_name: All Other Amusement and Recreation Industries
description: This industry provides recreational and amusement services (excluding amusement parks/arcades, gambling, golf courses/country clubs, skiing, marinas, fitness centers, bowling centers). It includes amusement ride/nongambling device concession operators, miniature golf, driving ranges, shooting ranges, recreational camps, billiard parlors, and escape rooms.

This sector provides lodging and/or prepares meals, snacks, and beverages for immediate consumption. It includes hotels, motels, recreational camps, rooming houses, and various food service establishments like restaurants, caterers, and mobile food vendors.

This subsector provides lodging or short-term accommodations for travelers and others. It includes hotels, motels, resort hotels, bed-and-breakfast inns, RV parks, campgrounds, and longer-term facilities like rooming houses and workers' camps.

This industry group provides short-term lodging in hotels, motels, resort hotels, casino hotels, and bed-and-breakfast inns. Establishments may offer additional services like food, recreation, and conference facilities.

This industry provides short-term lodging in hotels, motor hotels, resort hotels, and motels (excluding casino hotels). Establishments may offer food/beverage, recreational services, conference rooms, laundry, and parking.

This industry provides short-term lodging in hotel facilities with an on-premises casino (table wagering, slot machines, sports betting). These establishments generally offer a range of services and amenities like food/beverage, entertainment, and conference facilities.

This industry provides short-term lodging in private homes or small converted buildings known as bed-and-breakfast inns. Services feature highly personalized service and include a full breakfast in the room rate.

This industry provides short-term lodging (excluding hotels, motels, casino hotels, and bed-and-breakfast inns). Examples include guest houses, tourist homes, housekeeping cabins/cottages, and hostels.

formal_name: RV (Recreational Vehicle) Parks and Recreational Camps
description: This industry group operates RV parks, campgrounds, and recreational/vacation camps (excluding instructional, day). These facilities accommodate campers, offer accommodation (cabins, fixed campsites), and provide amenities like food services and recreational activities.

formal_name: RV (Recreational Vehicle) Parks and Recreational Camps
description: RV (Recreational Vehicle) Parks and Recreational Camps

This industry operates sites accommodating campers and their equipment (tents, tent trailers, travel trailers, RVs). Establishments may provide access to facilities like washrooms, laundry rooms, recreation halls, playgrounds, stores, and snack bars.

This industry operates overnight recreational camps (e.g., children's camps, family vacation camps, hunting/fishing camps, outdoor adventure retreats) offering activities like trail riding, white water rafting, hiking. Facilities provide accommodation (cabins, fixed campsites), food, and organized recreational activities.

formal_name: Rooming and Boarding Houses, Dormitories, and Workers' Camps
description: This industry group operates rooming and boarding houses, dormitories, and similar facilities like fraternity/sorority houses and workers' camps. These establishments provide temporary or longer-term accommodations that may serve as a principal residence, optionally with housekeeping, meals, and laundry.

formal_name: Rooming and Boarding Houses, Dormitories, and Workers' Camps
description: Rooming and Boarding Houses, Dormitories, and Workers' Camps

formal_name: Rooming and Boarding Houses, Dormitories, and Workers' Camps
description: This industry operates rooming/boarding houses and similar facilities (e.g., fraternity/sorority houses, off-campus dormitories, workers' camps). These establishments provide temporary or longer-term accommodations that may serve as a principal residence, optionally with housekeeping, meals, and laundry services.

This subsector prepares meals, snacks, and beverages for immediate consumption, on-premises or off-premises. Industries are grouped by service type, including food service contractors, caterers, mobile food services, drinking places, and various restaurants.

This industry group provides food services at customer locations, designated locations, or from motorized/nonmotorized vehicles. It includes food service contractors (e.g., airline, cafeteria, concession) and caterers for single event-based food services.

This industry provides food services at institutional, governmental, commercial, or industrial locations based on contractual arrangements. Services are for the convenience of the contracting organization/customers, with management staff always provided by the contractor.

This industry provides single event-based food services, typically transporting meals/snacks to events and/or preparing food off-premise. Banquet halls with catering staff are included, catering events like graduation parties, wedding receptions, and trade shows.

This industry prepares and serves meals/snacks for immediate consumption from motorized vehicles or nonmotorized carts (e.g., hot dog carts, ice cream trucks). The establishment is the central location for servicing the route.

This industry group operates establishments known as bars, taverns, nightclubs, or drinking places, primarily preparing and serving alcoholic beverages for immediate consumption. Limited food services may also be provided.

This industry operates establishments known as bars, taverns, nightclubs, or drinking places, primarily preparing and serving alcoholic beverages for immediate consumption. Limited food services may also be provided.

This industry group provides food services to patrons who order and are served while seated, or who order/select items and pay before eating. It includes full-service, limited-service, cafeterias, grill buffets, and snack/nonalcoholic beverage bars.

This industry provides food services where patrons order and are served while seated, paying after eating. These establishments may also sell alcoholic beverages, provide carryout, or present live nontheatrical entertainment.

This industry provides food services (excluding snack/nonalcoholic beverage bars) where patrons order/select items and pay before eating. Food/drink can be consumed on premises, taken out, or delivered. Some establishments may also sell alcoholic beverages.

This industry, known as cafeterias, grill buffets, or buffets, prepares and serves meals for immediate consumption using cafeteria-style or buffet serving equipment. Patrons select food/drink from displays in a continuous line or from buffet stations.

This industry prepares and/or serves specialty snacks (e.g., ice cream, frozen yogurt, cookies, popcorn) or nonalcoholic beverages (e.g., coffee, juices, sodas) for consumption on or near premises. Establishments may also sell related products, promoting a unique snack or beverage.

This sector covers a wide range of services not classified elsewhere, including equipment and machinery repair, religious activities, grantmaking, advocacy, personal care, death care, pet care, photofinishing, parking, and household employment. Excludes retailing equipment with repairs.

This subsector restores and maintains machinery, equipment, and other products to working order, categorizing by the type of repair activity. It includes automotive, electronic, commercial/industrial machinery, and personal/household goods repair, excluding repair done by manufacturers or construction trades.

This industry group provides repair and maintenance services for automotive vehicles and trailers. It includes general mechanical/electrical repair, engine repair/replacement, body/paint/interior/glass repair, oil change/lubrication, and car washing.

formal_name: Automotive Mechanical and Electrical Repair and Maintenance
description: Automotive Mechanical and Electrical Repair and Maintenance

This industry provides a wide range of mechanical and electrical repair/maintenance services for automotive vehicles (passenger cars, trucks, vans) and trailers, or performs engine repair/replacement. Examples include auto repair garages and engine repair shops.

This industry provides specialized mechanical or electrical repair/maintenance services (excluding engine repair/replacement) for automotive vehicles and trailers. Examples include automotive brake repair, suspension repair, exhaust system replacement, electrical repair, transmission repair, and tune-up shops.

formal_name: Other Automotive Mechanical and Electrical Repair and Maintenance
description: Other Automotive Mechanical and Electrical Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Automotive Body, Paint, Interior, and Glass Repair
description: Automotive Body, Paint, Interior, and Glass Repair

formal_name: Automotive Body, Paint, and Interior Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry repairs or customizes automotive vehicle/trailer bodies and interiors, and/or paints automotive vehicles/trailer bodies. It includes automotive body shops, body conversion services, paint shops, and restoration of antique/classic automotive vehicles.
This industry replaces, repairs, and/or tints automotive vehicle glass, e.g., for passenger cars, trucks, and vans.

formal_name: Automotive Oil Change and Lubrication Shops
description: This industry changes motor oil and lubricates the chassis of automotive vehicles (passenger cars, trucks, vans).
This industry cleans, washes, and/or waxes automotive vehicles (passenger cars, trucks, vans) and trailers. It includes automotive detail shops, mobile car/truck washes, and self-service car washes.

formal_name: All Other Automotive Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry provides automotive repair/maintenance services (excluding mechanical/electrical repair, body/paint/interior/glass repair, oil change/lubrication, and car washing) for automotive vehicles and trailers. Examples include automotive air-conditioning repair and rustproofing shops.

formal_name: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry group repairs and maintains consumer electronic equipment, computers, office machines, communication equipment, and other electronic/precision equipment/instruments, without retailing new products. Services cover items like microscopes, radar, televisions, and medical equipment.

formal_name: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance
description: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Electronic and Precision Equipment Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry repairs/maintains consumer electronic equipment, computers, office machines, communication equipment, and other electronic/precision equipment/instruments, without retailing these products as new. Items include microscopes, radar, televisions, stereos, computers, fax machines, and medical equipment.

formal_name: Computer and Office Machine Repair and Maintenance
description: Computer and Office Machine Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry group repairs and maintains commercial and industrial machinery and equipment. Services include sharpening/installing blades/saws, welding, and repairing agricultural, heavy, and industrial machinery, e.g., forklifts, machine tools, and commercial refrigeration equipment.

formal_name: Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance
description: Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Commercial and Industrial Machinery and Equipment (except Automotive and Electronic) Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry repairs/maintains commercial/industrial machinery and equipment. It sharpens/installs commercial/industrial machinery blades/saws, provides welding repair, or repairs agricultural/heavy/industrial machinery (e.g., forklifts, machine tools, commercial refrigeration equipment, construction equipment, mining machinery).

formal_name: Personal and Household Goods Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry group repairs and services home/garden equipment, household appliances, reupholsters/repairs furniture, and fixes footwear/leather goods. It also covers other personal/household goods like garments, watches, jewelry, musical instruments, and recreational boats.

formal_name: Home and Garden Equipment and Appliance Repair and Maintenance
description: Home and Garden Equipment and Appliance Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Home and Garden Equipment Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry repairs/services home and garden equipment without retailing new items, e.g., lawnmowers, handheld power tools, edgers, snowblowers, leaf blowers, and trimmers.
This industry repairs/services household appliances without retailing new appliances, e.g., refrigerators, stoves, washing machines, clothes dryers, and room air-conditioners.
This industry reupholsters, refinishes, repairs, and/or restores furniture.
This industry repairs footwear and/or other leather/leather-like goods (e.g., handbags, briefcases) without retailing new footwear/leather goods.

formal_name: Other Personal and Household Goods Repair and Maintenance
description: Other Personal and Household Goods Repair and Maintenance

formal_name: Other Personal and Household Goods Repair and Maintenance
description: This industry repairs/services personal or household-type goods (excluding home/garden equipment, appliances, furniture, and footwear/leather goods) without retailing new items. It includes repairing garments, watches, jewelry, musical instruments, bicycles/motorcycles, and recreational boats.

This subsector provides personal and laundry services to individuals, households, and businesses. Services include personal care (e.g., hair, nail, skin), death care, drycleaning, laundry, pet care, photofinishing, temporary parking, and dating services.

This industry group provides appearance care services to individual consumers, e.g., hair, nail, and skin care services, permanent makeup, ear piercing, hair replacement/weaving, tanning, and tattoo parlors. Also includes non-medical diet and weight reducing centers.

formal_name: Hair, Nail, and Skin Care Services
description: Hair, Nail, and Skin Care Services
This industry, known as barber shops or men's hair stylist shops, primarily cuts, trims, and styles men's/boys' hair, and/or shaves and trims men's beards.

This industry (excluding barber shops) cuts, trims, shampoos, colors, waves, or styles hair; provides facials; and/or applies makeup (excluding permanent makeup). Examples include beauty parlors, hairdressing salons, and cosmetology salons.
This industry provides nail care services, e.g., manicures, pedicures, and nail extensions.

This industry provides non-medical services to assist clients in attaining/maintaining desired weight. Services typically include individual/group counseling, menu/exercise planning, and weight/body measurement monitoring, often integrating weight reduction product sales.

This industry provides personal care services (excluding hair, nail, facial, nonpermanent makeup, or non-medical diet/weight reducing services). Examples include day spas, depilatory/electrolysis salons, ear piercing, hair replacement/weaving, tanning salons, and tattoo parlors.

This industry group prepares the dead for burial/interment, conducts funerals (providing facilities, arranging transportation, selling caskets), operates sites/structures for human/animal remains interment, and/or cremates the dead.

This industry prepares the dead for burial/interment and conducts funerals (providing facilities for wakes, arranging transportation, selling caskets). Funeral homes combined with crematories are included.
This industry operates sites/structures reserved for human/animal remains interment and/or cremates the dead. It includes cemetery associations, memorial gardens, pet cemeteries, and mausoleums.

This industry group operates coin- or card-operated self-service laundries/drycleaners, provides drycleaning/laundering services, offers drop-off/pick-up sites, and supplies/services laundered items (e.g., uniforms, linens) on a rental/contract basis.

This industry operates facilities with coin- or card-operated self-service laundry/drycleaning equipment for customer use on premises, and/or supplies/services such equipment for customer use in other businesses like apartments and dormitories.

This industry provides drycleaning (excluding coin-operated), laundering (excluding linen/uniform supply, coin-operated), drop-off/pick-up sites, and/or specialty cleaning for garments/textile items (excluding carpets/upholstery). Services may be performed on-premises, off-premises, or both.
This industry supplies, on a rental or contract basis, laundered items like table/bed linens, towels, diapers, and uniforms/gowns/coats for various professions.

This industry supplies, on a rental or contract basis, laundered industrial work uniforms, related work clothing (e.g., protective apparel, clean room apparel), and dust control items (e.g., treated mops, rugs, mats, shop towels).

This industry group provides personal services (excluding personal care, death care, drycleaning/laundry, pet care, photofinishing, parking). It includes bail bonding, shoeshine, coin/card-operated personal services machine operations, social escort services, consumer buying, and wedding planning.
This industry provides pet care services (excluding veterinary), e.g., boarding, grooming, sitting, walking, and training pets.
This industry (excluding "one-hour" photofinishing labs) develops film and/or makes photographic slides, prints, and enlargements.
This industry, known as "one-hour" photofinishing labs, develops film and/or makes photographic slides, prints, and enlargements on a short turnaround or while-you-wait basis.
This industry provides parking space for motor vehicles, usually on an hourly, daily, or monthly basis, and/or valet parking services.

This industry provides personal services (excluding personal care, death care, drycleaning/laundry, pet care, photofinishing, or parking/valet services). Examples include bail bonding, shoeshine services, coin-operated personal services machine operations, social escort services, consumer buying, and wedding planning.

formal_name: Religious, Grantmaking, Civic, Professional, and Similar Organizations
description: This subsector groups establishments organizing religious activities, supporting causes through grantmaking, advocating social/political causes, and promoting/defending members' interests. Industry groups are defined by activities like funding causes, advocacy, and membership-based organizations.
This industry group operates religious organizations (churches, temples, mosques, monasteries) and/or administers organized religions or promotes religious activities.
This industry operates religious organizations (e.g., churches, temples, mosques, monasteries) and/or administers organized religions or promotes religious activities.

This industry group awards grants from trust funds (grantmaking foundations, charitable trusts) and/or raises funds for social welfare activities (health, educational, scientific, cultural), including community chests and federated charities.

This industry comprises grantmaking foundations or charitable trusts that award grants from trust funds (based on competitive selection or grantor preferences), or fund a single entity. It includes community foundations, philanthropic trusts, corporate foundations, and scholarship trusts.
This industry raises funds for health-related research, e.g., disease prevention (heart, cancer, diabetes), health education, and patient services.

This industry (excluding voluntary health organizations) raises funds for a wide range of social welfare activities, e.g., educational, scientific, cultural, and health. It includes community chest fundraising organizations, federated charities, and united fund councils.

This industry group promotes particular causes or specific social/political goals for broad or specific constituencies. It includes human rights, environmental protection/conservation/wildlife organizations, and other social advocacy (e.g., peace, substance abuse prevention).

This industry promotes human rights causes for broad or specific constituencies, addressing issues like constitutional rights, civil liberties, protection of vulnerable groups, intergroup relations, and voter education. These organizations may solicit contributions and offer memberships.

This industry promotes environmental and wildlife preservation/protection. It addresses issues like clean air/water, global warming, natural resource conservation/development, and protecting wildlife/endangered species. Organizations may solicit contributions and offer memberships.

This industry engages in social advocacy (excluding human rights and environmental protection/conservation/wildlife preservation). It addresses issues like peace, international understanding, community action (excluding civic organizations), and advancing social causes (e.g., firearms safety, drunk driving prevention, drug abuse awareness).

This industry group promotes civic and social interests of its members, e.g., alumni associations, automobile clubs (excluding travel), booster clubs, ethnic associations, fraternal lodges, parent-teacher associations, and veterans' membership organizations.

This industry promotes civic and social interests of its members, e.g., alumni associations, automobile clubs (excluding travel), booster clubs, ethnic associations, fraternal lodges, parent-teacher associations, scouting organizations, social clubs, and veterans' membership organizations.

formal_name: Business, Professional, Labor, Political, and Similar Organizations
description: This industry group promotes members' interests (excluding religious, social advocacy, civic/social organizations). It includes business associations, professional organizations, labor unions, and political organizations, which may conduct research, develop statistics, lobby officials, or publish newsletters.

This industry promotes the business interests of its members. Activities include research on new products/services, market statistics, quality/certification standards, lobbying, and publishing newsletters/books/periodicals for members.

This industry promotes professional interests of its members and the profession as a whole. Activities include research, statistics, quality/certification standards, lobbying, and publishing newsletters/books/periodicals for members.

formal_name: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
description: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations

formal_name: Labor Unions and Similar Labor Organizations
description: This industry promotes the interests of organized labor and union employees.
This industry promotes the interests of national, state, or local political parties or candidates. It includes political groups organized to raise funds for parties or individual candidates.

formal_name: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
description: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)

formal_name: Other Similar Organizations (except Business, Professional, Labor, and Political Organizations)
description: This industry promotes members' interests (excluding religious, social advocacy, civic/social, business associations, professional organizations, labor unions, and political organizations). Examples include athletic associations/leagues (regulatory), condominium/homeowners' associations, and property/tenants'/cooperative owners' associations.
This subsector includes private households employing workers on or about the premises for household operation, e.g., cooks, maids, nannies, gardeners, and other maintenance staff.

This industry group comprises private households employing workers on or about the premises for household operation, e.g., cooks, maids, nannies, butlers, non-medical personal care aides, gardeners, and maintenance workers.

This industry comprises private households primarily employing workers on or about the premises for household operation, e.g., cooks, maids, nannies, butlers, non-medical personal care aides, gardeners, caretakers, and other maintenance workers.
State-level government entities tracked by WHD.

This sector consists of government agencies (federal, state, local) that administer public programs with executive, legislative, or judicial authority. Activities include setting policy, creating laws, adjudicating cases, and providing public safety/national defense, generally for programs not performed by private establishments.

formal_name: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support
description: This subsector groups offices of government executives, legislative bodies, public finance, and general government support functions. It includes central administrative offices, legislative commissions, and agencies providing general government support.

formal_name: Executive, Legislative, and Other General Government Support
description: This industry group serves as offices of chief executives, legislative bodies, and their advisory committees/commissions. It includes public finance, taxation, monetary policy, debt/investment administration, auditing, and government employee retirement trust fund administration.
This industry comprises government establishments serving as offices of chief executives and their advisory committees/commissions, e.g., offices of the president, governors, and mayors.

This industry comprises government establishments serving as legislative bodies and their advisory committees/commissions, e.g., Congress, state legislatures, and advisory/study legislative commissions.

This industry includes government establishments primarily engaged in public finance, taxation, and monetary policy. Activities cover financial administration, tax administration/collection, fund custody/disbursement, debt/investment administration, auditing, and government employee retirement trust fund administration.

This industry comprises government establishments serving as councils/boards of commissioners or supervisors where the chief executive (e.g., county executive, city mayor) is a member of the legislative body.

formal_name: American Indian and Alaska Native Tribal Governments
description: American Indian and Alaska Native Tribal Governments

formal_name: American Indian and Alaska Native Tribal Governments
description: This industry comprises American Indian and Alaska Native governing bodies performing legislative, judicial, and administrative functions for their lands. It includes tribal councils, courts, and law enforcement.

This industry comprises government establishments primarily providing general support for government (excluding elsewhere classified public administration). Services include personnel services, election boards, civil rights commissions, and supply agencies.

formal_name: Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities
description: This industry group involves government establishments administering justice, public order, and safety programs. It includes civilian courts, police protection, legal counsel/prosecution, correctional institutions, parole/probation offices, and fire protection.

This industry comprises civilian courts of law (excluding American Indian and Alaska Native tribal courts). It includes civilian courts, courts of law, and sheriffs' offices performing court functions only.

This industry comprises government establishments primarily engaged in criminal/civil law enforcement, police, traffic safety, and related activities for law enforcement/order preservation. Combined police and fire departments are included.

This industry comprises government establishments primarily providing legal counsel or prosecution services for the government. Examples include attorney generals' offices, district attorneys' offices, and public defenders'/prosecutors' offices.

This industry comprises government establishments primarily managing/operating correctional institutions (e.g., penitentiaries, detention centers, prisons, jails) for the confinement, correction, and rehabilitation of adult and/or juvenile offenders.
This industry comprises government establishments judicially administering probation offices, parole offices and boards, and pardon boards.

This industry comprises government establishments primarily engaged in firefighting and other related fire protection activities. Government establishments providing combined fire protection and ambulance or rescue services are included.

formal_name: Other Justice, Public Order, and Safety Activities
description: This industry comprises government establishments in public order and safety (excluding courts, police, legal counsel/prosecution, correctional, parole/probation, fire protection). It includes general administration of public order/safety programs, consumer product safety commissions, and emergency planning/management offices.

This subsector groups government establishments administering human resource programs, including education, public health, and veterans' affairs. It covers planning, supervision, and coordination of these social programs.

This industry group involves government establishments planning, administering, and coordinating human resource programs, e.g., education, public health, and veterans' affairs. It includes social security, disability insurance, Medicare, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation programs.

This industry comprises government establishments centrally coordinating, planning, supervising, and administering funds, policies, intergovernmental activities, statistical reports, data collection, and centralized programs for educational administration. Government scholarship programs are included.

This industry comprises government establishments planning, administering, and coordinating public health programs/services, including environmental health, mental health, categorical health programs, health statistics, and immunization services. It includes public health-related inspections and coroners' offices.

formal_name: Administration of Human Resource Programs (except Education, Public Health, and Veterans' Affairs Programs)
description: This industry comprises government establishments planning, administering, and coordinating programs for public assistance, social work, and welfare activities. It includes the administration of Social Security, disability insurance, Medicare, unemployment insurance, and workers' compensation programs.

This industry comprises government establishments administering programs of assistance, training, counseling, and other services to veterans and their dependents/heirs/survivors. It includes Veterans' Affairs offices that liaise and coordinate with other service organizations and government agencies.

This subsector groups government establishments administering environmental quality programs. It focuses on regulating air/water resources, solid waste, pollution control, flood control, drainage development, toxic waste cleanup, and coordinating these activities.

This industry group includes government establishments administering, regulating, and enforcing air/water resource programs, solid waste management, pollution control, flood control, drainage development, toxic waste removal, and coordinating these activities.

description: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs

formal_name: Administration of Air and Water Resource and Solid Waste Management Programs
description: This industry administers, regulates, and enforces air/water resource programs; administers/regulates solid waste management, water/air pollution control/prevention, flood control, drainage development, water resource consumption, and toxic waste removal/cleanup programs; and coordinates these activities at intergovernmental levels.

This industry administers, regulates, supervises, and controls land use (including recreational areas); conserves/preserves natural resources (erosion control, geological survey); administers weather forecasting programs; and protects public/private forest lands. It also plans/manages/regulates game, fish, and wildlife populations.

formal_name: Administration of Housing Programs, Urban Planning, and Community Development
description: This industry group involves government establishments administering and planning housing programs, urban planning, and community/rural development. It includes land redevelopment agencies, regional planning, and zoning boards.
This industry comprises government establishments primarily engaged in the administration and planning of housing programs.

description: Administration of Urban Planning and Community and Rural Development

formal_name: Administration of Urban Planning and Community and Rural Development
description: This industry comprises government establishments administering and planning urban/rural area development, including land redevelopment agencies, regional planning, and zoning boards/commissions.

This industry group includes government establishments administering, promoting, and developing economic resources, e.g., business, industry, and tourism. It covers general statistical data, economic well-being, and regulation/licensing/inspection of various commercial sectors.

This industry comprises government establishments administering, promoting, and developing economic resources, e.g., business, industry, and tourism. It covers general statistical data, economic well-being, consumer protection, and small business development.

formal_name: Regulation and Administration of Transportation Programs
description: This industry comprises government establishments administering, regulating, licensing, planning, inspecting, and investigating transportation services and facilities. It includes motor vehicle/operator licensing, the Coast Guard (excluding academy), and parking authorities.

formal_name: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
description: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities

formal_name: Regulation and Administration of Communications, Electric, Gas, and Other Utilities
description: This industry comprises government establishments administering, regulating, licensing, and inspecting utilities, e.g., communications, electric power (fossil, nuclear, solar, water, wind), gas, water supply, and sewerage.

description: Regulation of Agricultural Marketing and Commodities

formal_name: Regulation of Agricultural Marketing and Commodities
description: This industry comprises government establishments planning, administering, and coordinating agricultural programs for production, marketing, and utilization, including educational/promotional activities. It regulates/controls grading and inspection of food, plants, animals, and other agricultural products.

formal_name: Regulation, Licensing, and Inspection of Miscellaneous Commercial Sectors
description: This industry comprises government establishments regulating, licensing, and inspecting commercial sectors, e.g., retail trade, professional occupations, manufacturing, mining, construction, and services. It maintains physical standards, regulates hazardous conditions, and enforces alcoholic beverage control regulations.
This industry group comprises government establishments administering and operating space flights, space research, and space exploration, including space flight centers.
This industry comprises government establishments administering and operating space flights, space research, and space exploration, including space flight centers.
This subsector groups government establishments focusing on national security (Armed Forces, National Guard) and international affairs, including programs relating to other nations and peoples.

This industry group includes government establishments of the Armed Forces and National Guard focusing on national security, and establishments primarily engaged in international affairs and programs relating to other nations.

This industry comprises government establishments of the Armed Forces, including the National Guard, primarily engaged in national security and related activities, e.g., military police, military training schools (excluding academies), and military courts.
This industry comprises establishments of U.S. and foreign governments primarily engaged in international affairs and programs relating to other nations and peoples.
